name: Aiwan-e-Sadr (President House), public exterior only
assumptions: No published height: stage heights fitted to one long-lens front photo, scaled by the 4.9 m slot rhythm and the 134 m front width; roof at 36.9 m, flag masts to about 43 m.
Esri imagery leans about 31 degrees toward the front; every roof position was corrected by 0.6 m per metre of height, so ground positions carry an error of a few metres.
Front range wall treated as sitting on level ground at z 0; the real site drops in steps toward Constitution Avenue, which is not modelled.
Cladding colour is a photo estimate of off-white; no source documents the material.
Side elevations of the upper stages were not photographed clearly: the window positions on them are guesses.
Rear elevation of the upper stages is built the same as the front (not seen directly).
Rear range heights, window positions and the 3.4 m column spacing are read from one oblique garden-side photo.
Side wings at 11 m and the skylit spine at 4 m are estimates: neither is visible from a side in any photo found.
Rear pavilion walls and the height of their pyramid roofs are guesses; only the terracotta plan squares are seen, from above.
Blue skylights drawn as flat panels; the round fittings seen in the imagery are left out.
Two flag masts on the cap are placed from the front photos; flags are not modelled.
Gardens, fountains, trees, the solar fields to the SE and all security features are outside this model.
Night glow values are placeholders: lighting is undocumented.
